requirements: At least two exact primary, authoritative, or scholarly locators
Clear differentiation from existing catalog records
No unresolved translation, source-metadata, lineage, or community-governance blocker

records.name: Oyěwùmí's seniority-centered critique of gendered social personhood
records.differentiation: The existing Yorùbá person-components record addresses ara, ẹ̀mí, orí, and ọkàn; this proposal instead tracks a historically specific argument about seniority, social classification, and colonial gender categories.
records.boundary: Limit to Oyěwùmí's reconstruction of precolonial Ọ̀yọ́-Yorùbá society, record the published critique, and do not generalize to all Yorùbá people, all African societies, or the absence of gender everywhere.

citations.title: The Invention of Women: Making an African Sense of Western Gender Discourses
Yorubas Don't Do Gender: A Critical Review of Oyèrónkẹ́ Oyěwùmí's The Invention of Women

records.name: Ambedkar's anti-caste account of socially degraded selfhood and democratic self-respect
records.differentiation: No current catalog record treats caste as a structure of graded inequality shaping agency, social recognition, self-respect, fraternity, and associated democratic life.
records.boundary: Keep the claim within Ambedkar's anti-caste and Dalit political philosophy; do not present it as a general South Asian metaphysics of self or reduce caste to class, race, status, or stigma.

citations.title: Ambedkar's Political Philosophy: A Grammar of Public Life from the Social Margins

records.name: Kohn's ecology of selves
records.differentiation: The catalog contains Amerindian perspectivism and Hallowell's Northern Ojibwe account, but not Kohn's Peircean semiotic anthropology of nonhuman selfhood based on Runa-grounded fieldwork.
records.boundary: Label this as Eduardo Kohn's anthropological construction, not a direct or timeless statement of Runa doctrine, a pan-Amazonian view, or an identity claim about perspectivism.

citations.title: How Forests Think: Toward an Anthropology Beyond the Human

records.name: Descola's four modes of identification
records.differentiation: The catalog has particular ethnographic and perspectivist records but not Descola's explicit comparative typology of animism, naturalism, totemism, and analogism via interiority and physicality.
records.boundary: Present these as the analyst's ideal types rather than community self-descriptions, exhaustive cultures, cognitive modules, or evolutionary stages.

citations.title: Beyond Nature and Culture
citations.authors: Philippe Descola; translated by Janet Lloyd

citations.title: Modes of Being and Forms of Predication

records.name: Beauvoir's situated, embodied, and ambiguous subjectivity
records.differentiation: No current record integrates Beauvoir's account of embodied freedom, oppression, social Othering, ambiguity, and situated agency.
records.boundary: Do not universalize 'woman,' reduce ambiguity to uncertainty, or omit the historical, racial, and colonial limitations identified in Beauvoir scholarship.

citations.title: Simone de Beauvoir and the Politics of Ambiguity

records.name: Lugones's world-traveling and plural self
records.differentiation: The catalog lacks Lugones's technical account of differently constituted social worlds, plural selfhood, playful perception, and resistant coalition.
records.boundary: Retain its Latina and Women-of-Color feminist genealogy. A 'world' is a technical social-experiential construction, and plural selfhood is not dissociative identity or code-switching alone.

citations.title: Pilgrimages/Peregrinajes: Theorizing Coalition against Multiple Oppressions

records.name: Milton's Double Empathy Problem
records.differentiation: The catalog includes interaction theory and the submentalizing challenge, but not Milton's autistic-led account of reciprocal experiential and communicative mismatch.
records.boundary: Do not infer that all mismatches are symmetric, that individual impairments never exist, or that autistic people do not require support and accommodation.

citations.title: On the Ontological Status of Autism: The 'Double Empathy Problem'
The 'Double Empathy Problem': Ten Years On
citations.authors: Damian Milton, Emine Gurbuz, and Beatriz López

records.name: Neurodiversity paradigm
records.differentiation: No current record explicitly separates neurodiversity as a fact of variation, the neurodiversity movement, and the neurodiversity paradigm's normative interpretation of mind, disability, and environment.
records.boundary: Credit collective autistic-community origins. Do not treat the paradigm as a unitary empirical theory or claim that it denies impairment, disability, high support needs, care, or intervention.

citations.title: The Neurodiversity Concept Was Developed Collectively: An Overdue Correction on the Origins of Neurodiversity Theory
citations.authors: Monique Botha, Robert Chapman, Morénike Giwa Onaiwu, Steven K. Kapp, Abs Stannard Ashley, and Nick Walker
